Weeks would turn into months.
On the coast, the sea would hold out the longest.
Oceans store enormous amounts of heat, so the shore would cool more slowly than the land.
But the beach would freeze solid, and the waves would turn thick and slow.
Then a crust of ice would spread across the water.
Each week, the ice would grow a little thicker and push farther out to sea.
On land, most plants would be dead within weeks.
Only the biggest trees could hold on longer, living off the sugar stored in their trunks.
Minus thirty.
Most animals would run out of food.
Without sunlight, no crop could grow anywhere on the surface.
People would survive only where they had power, fuel and shelter.
Some would move underground, where the rock keeps the temperature steady.
Places with hot springs and volcanoes, like Iceland, could live on the heat of the Earth itself.
Cities would shrink to a few warm islands of light in an endless dark.
With almost no water left to evaporate, the clouds would thin out and the snow would stop.
Just a clear, black sky.
Minus fifty.
Out on the frozen sea, nothing would move.
Not a wave.
Not a breath of wind.
Just the crack of ice, settling in the dark.
